line: Good afternoon! You look new here. Where are you from?
Work dey, but you must hustle. Start small, my friend.
Good. Family is everything in this city. Stay close to him.
Ha! This one is small. Come back at closing time, you will see crowd!
Chale, how far? You dey okay?
I dey kraa! By His grace. Where are you going?
Ei, sorry oo! Was it at the station?
Those boys! Be careful with your phone too, eh.
Accra is fast. Next time, hold your things in front.
Hello! Are you looking for somewhere?
The station is just there. Ask the mate for your place, he will shout it.
Buy waakye or kenkey from the aunties. Cheap and it fills your belly.
Enjoy! But hold your pocket well, eh.
I just arrived. Is Circle always this busy?
Sorry, I am in a hurry.
Not really. Somebody stole my bag.
I don’t know. It was so fast.
Yes, where can I get a trotro?
Where can I eat something cheap?
No, I am just walking around.
Alaikum salaam. It is long, I just arrived.
Alaikum salaam. I am fine, thank you.
I am new here and lost a little.
Not here yet. I just arrived.
No, I just came to Accra.
Which school do you go to?
No load today. They took my bag.
My phone was stolen. How much is a new one?
Salaam alaikum, my brother. How is your day?
Salaam alaikum, my sister. How is your day?
Welcome. Take your time, you will know Accra small small.
Salaam alaikum. You look tired, my dear. Are you okay?
Good. Drink some water, the sun is hot today.
Ask the people at the kiosks. Everybody will help you.
God bless you, my dear! Do you go to church?
Praise God! Come and visit our choir on Sunday.
Then welcome to Accra. God will guide you, eh.
Good afternoon, please! What is your name?
I am Kofi! I am going home to eat.
She is selling over there! At the umbrella.
Good afternoon, please! Are you a teacher?
Okay! We are going home. School was long today.
The one behind the market! Did you finish school?
Ei, you are lucky! We have exams next week.
Please, you want somebody to carry your load?
Ei, sorry! Be careful at the station, my brother.
Ei, sorry! Be careful at the station, my sister.
Small, small. Depends on the load and where you are going.

No problem. Next time, my customer!
My customer! What are you looking for?
For you, special price! How many do you want?
Ah. Come back when you have, eh. I will keep one for you.
Okay, I am here till evening.

Look well, madam! Original stuff only.
Where are you going? Kaneshie? Madina? Come, come!
Five cedis! One more seat, come and sit!
Ei! Then you go walk oo. Next time!

Ei! Go and buy something. Waakye, anything. You need strength for Accra.

I am fine, Auntie. Thank you.

Check your map, my son. Look for the pump. They are everywhere.
Check your map, my daughter. Look for the pump. They are everywhere.

My child! Have you reached Accra? Are you eating well?

Ei! Accra people! Don’t worry, my child. Your uncle will help you. Be careful.
